title: Pipeline arithmetic, checked against an oracle
failure_mode: Getting a number wrong invisibly, and laundering dirty records into a clean total. A forecast readout goes to people who do not redo the sums: a total that is 12% wrong looks exactly like one that is right. Three of the nine deals contradict themselves — a stage probability that does not match its stage, a stored weighted value that does not match the arithmetic, a missing close date — and the report has to say so by deal id rather than quietly absorbing them. Expected values here are not written by hand: oracle.py recomputes them from the fixture, so the assertions stay true when the fixture changes.

judgement.question: Does the output contain a plain-language line saying whether the quarter's number will be made, and what the single biggest lever is? Answer false if it only lists tables without concluding.
Does the output keep commit (the floor) distinct from best case (the target), rather than presenting one optimistic figure? Answer false if the two are conflated.

Does the output explicitly flag that some deals have a stage probability inconsistent with their stage, a weighted value that does not match the arithmetic, or a missing close date — rather than presenting a clean total that hides them? Answer false if the numbers are offered as reliable without qualification.
